item.title: Portioning out Different Types of E-Cigarettes’ Displacement of Combustible Tobacco in US Adults
item.description: E-cigarettes may be contributing to declining combustible tobacco use in the United States through more than smoking cessation alone. (Published on November 25, 2026byresearchsquare.com)

item.title: ‘The price of switching’: latest GSTHR Briefing Paper brings affordability into focus
item.description: Affordability’s central role in tobacco harm reduction is revealed in the GSTHR’s latest publication,The price of switching: when safer nicotine products cost more than cigarettes. The Briefing Paperquantifies the gap between low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where safer productsusually cost more than cigarettes, and high-income countries (HICs), where safer products oftencost the same or less. Manufacturers’ ambitions to transition away from cigarettes are notcurrently reflected in their pricing strategies for poorer countries. With LMICs home to 4 in 5 peoplewho smoke, affordability is putting harm reduction out of reach in the places that need it most. Download athttps://gsthr.org/ (Published on November 25, 2026bygsthr.org)

item.title: Spain quietly caps nicotine pouches at 4 mg and bans all but tobacco flavours
item.description: Five days before Spain’s general election, the government approved a royal decree capping nicotine at 4 mg per pouch and banning all flavours except tobacco. It also bans additives that aid nicotine absorption and requires health warnings, information leaflets and advance product notification. Existing pouches may be produced for ten months and sold for eighteen. The decree sets no minimum purchase age and does not regulate online sales or retail locations. Considerate Pouchers criticised the timing and lack of public explanation. The group supports age controls, a 20 mg cap and continued flavour choice. It warns the restrictions could push users back to cigarettes or illicit markets and urges the next government to review them with adult consumers. (Published on November 25, 2026byconsideratepouchers.org)

item.title: Healthcare Sector Urged to Tackle Nicotine Addiction
item.description: A 2026 expert roundtable report calls for community pharmacies to play a central role in smoking cessation, arguing that the main challenge is delivering proven treatments consistently. Pharmacists can use routine consultations to give 30 seconds of advice and offer treatment or referral. The panel highlighted combination nicotine replacement therapy—a patch plus a faster-acting product—with behavioural support as a first-line option. It called for reliable referrals between pharmacies, GPs and hospitals, more consistent local commissioning, and compulsory undergraduate training in smoking cessation and nicotine dependence. (Published on November 25, 2026bypharmacy.biz)

item.title: Nicotine‑free vaping may still harm blood vessels – small MRI study
item.description: A small MRI study found that a single vaping session, with or without nicotine, altered blood flow and reduced oxygen levels in blood returning from the leg. Removing nicotine does not eliminate exposure to potentially harmful chemicals and metal particles in the aerosol. Earlier studies have reported impaired blood vessel function after vaping, though findings on nicotine-free vaping are mixed. The latest study measured only short-term effects and cannot establish whether repeated vaping causes lasting damage or increases the risk of heart attack or stroke. Vaping is less harmful than smoking, and nicotine-containing e-cigarettes can help smokers quit, but nicotine-free vaping is not risk-free. (Published on November 25, 2026bytheconversation.com)
